info.title: Alerts
info.description:
# Introduction
The alerts API enables you to consume alerts from Cyberint programmatically. 

These API should enable you to retrieve alert relevant information.
# Authentication
Cyberint API uses API access tokens as the method of authorization. 

The access token must be provided as a cookie for each of the requests. 

The access token cookie format is as follow: access_token={access_token}
# Request and response formats
In general, Cyberint API uses HTTP requests with JSON arguments and JSON responses.
## File download endpoints
Urls for file download are valid for a few minutes only. 

Hence those urls must be used only to retrieve the file content at the time of generation. 

The generated temporary url should not be saved for future use.
## Date format
All dates in the API use UTC and are strings in the ISO 8601 format
## Alert data as json content
If the include_csv_attachments_as_json_content flag is set to true.

The jsons will be added under alert_data -> csv -> content

get.description:
Retrieve the raw intel item (historically referred to as 'indicator') attached to a specific alert.

    This endpoint provides access to the underlying intelligence data that triggered the alert creation.
    The raw intel item contains the original threat intelligence information, including metadata,
    detection context, and enrichment data that SOC engineers need for investigation and analysis.

    Use this endpoint when you need to:
    - Access the original threat intelligence data behind an alert
    - Investigate the source and context of the detected threat
    - Perform deeper analysis of the intelligence item for threat hunting
    - Extract technical indicators for correlation with other security tools

200.description: Retrieves the raw intel item (indicator) attached to the specified alert

put.description:
Update up to 100 alerts status. In case of updating the status to 'Close' the 'Closure reason' is required.

**Note**: When sending a request, whether for one alert or several note to send the right and relevant closure_reason.
- Value 'Asset irrelevant' relevant only for those alerts: automatic ASM issues, on company 3rd party credentials
exposed, and on company customer payment cards exposed.
- Value 'Asset belongs to org' relevant only for those alerts: active phishing,
look-alike, social media or brand impersonation, mobile app impersonation and fake job impersonation.
- Values 'asm_no_longer_detected' and 'asm_manually_closed' are system-reserved and cannot be used manually.

post.description:
Retrieves a page of leaked credentials for a single tenant, one row per record.
    Supports filtering, sorting, and cursor pagination. Results are ordered by the requested
    `sort` (default: Status, New first) with a stable internal tie-breaker.
    A cursor is only valid for the sort it was issued with.
    Passwords are masked unless `show_passwords=true`.
